title: Introduction to lwpls
text: query sample \(x_q\), similarity weight training sample \(x_i\) \[ \omega_i = \exp\left(-\frac{d_i}{\sigma_d \, \varphi}\right), \qquad d_i = \lVert x_i - x_q \rVert, \] \(\sigma_d\) standard deviation distances \(d_i\) \(\varphi > 0\) localization parameter. training data centered weighted means, PLS model num_comp components fitted using weights \(\omega_i\), query projected onto local model get prediction. two main hyperparameters therefore: num_comp: number PLS components local models; localization: small values make models local (nearest samples matter); large values make weights similar, LW-PLS tends global PLS model. Optionally, neighbors restricts local model nearest training samples (“KNN-LW” strategy compared original LW-PLS Lesnoff et al., 2020), similarity changes distances \(d_i\) measured (see Similarity indexes).

what: Regression: fat-free water content of meat from NIR spectra
title: Introduction to lwpls
text: meats data modeldata package contain 100 near-infrared absorbance values 215 meat samples. predict water content. model specification marks hyperparameters tuning. Since LW-PLS calculates local models prediction time, values num_comp obtained model, tune fits one model per value localization (“submodel trick”).  local models (small localization) quickly -fit, large values reproduce global PLS. best models lie . finalize workflow best parameters evaluate test set:
code: data(meats, package = "modeldata") meats <- meats[, !names(meats) %in% c("fat", "protein")]  set.seed(123) meats_split <- initial_split(meats, prop = 0.75) meats_train <- training(meats_split) meats_test <- testing(meats_split) meats_folds <- vfold_cv(meats_train, v = 5) lwpls_spec <-   lwpls(num_comp = tune(), localization = tune()) |>   set_mode("regression")  lwpls_wflow <- workflow(water ~ ., lwpls_spec)  lwpls_grid <- dials::grid_regular(   dials::num_comp(c(1, 15)),   localization(),   levels = c(num_comp = 15, localization = 8) )  lwpls_res <- tune_grid(   lwpls_wflow,   resamples = meats_folds,   grid = lwpls_grid,   metrics = metric_set(rmse, rsq) )  show_best(lwpls_res, metric = "rmse", n = 5) #> # A tibble: 5 × 8 #>   num_comp localization .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err .config           #>      <int>        <dbl> <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>             #> 1       10          0.5 rmse    standard    1.66     5   0.156 pre0_mod077_post0 #> 2       13          0.5 rmse    standard    1.68     5   0.198 pre0_mod101_post0 #> 3        9          0.5 rmse    standard    1.70     5   0.174 pre0_mod069_post0 #> 4        8          0.5 rmse    standard    1.71     5   0.184 pre0_mod061_post0 #> 5       12          0.5 rmse    standard    1.77     5   0.194 pre0_mod093_post0 autoplot(lwpls_res, metric = "rmse") +   scale_color_viridis_d(option = "mako", end = 0.9) +   theme_bw() best_params <- select_best(lwpls_res, metric = "rmse") best_params #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>   num_comp localization .config           #>      <int>        <dbl> <chr>             #> 1       10          0.5 pre0_mod077_post0  lwpls_final <-   lwpls_wflow |>   finalize_workflow(best_params) |>   last_fit(meats_split)  collect_metrics(lwpls_final) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   .metric .estimator .estimate .config         #>   <chr>   <chr>          <dbl> <chr>           #> 1 rmse    standard       1.38  pre0_mod0_post0 #> 2 rsq     standard       0.978 pre0_mod0_post0

title: Introduction to lwpls
text: default, similarity two samples based Euclidean distance (standardized) predictors, every predictor counts equally, whether related outcome. Covariance-based LW-PLS (CbLW-PLS; Hazama Kano, 2015) measures distances along covariance direction \(\Gamma = X^\top y / \lVert X^\top y \rVert\) training data instead, \[ d_i = \lVert \Gamma^\top (x_i - x_q) \rVert, \] predictors related outcome drive similarity. Use similarity = "covariance" select . Since best index depends data, can tuned together parameters similarity(): spectra, two indexes perform similarly. Hazama Kano found CbLW-PLS give best predictions two industrial applications, worth including tuning grid.
code: similarity_wflow <- workflow(   water ~ .,   lwpls(num_comp = tune(), localization = tune(), similarity = tune()) |>     set_mode("regression") )  similarity_grid <- dials::grid_regular(   dials::num_comp(c(1, 15)),   localization(),   similarity(),   levels = c(num_comp = 15, localization = 8, similarity = 2) )  similarity_res <- tune_grid(   similarity_wflow,   resamples = meats_folds,   grid = similarity_grid,   metrics = metric_set(rmse) )  # Best configuration of each similarity index similarity_perf <- collect_metrics(similarity_res) best_by_index <- lapply(   split(similarity_perf, similarity_perf$similarity),   function(x) x[which.min(x$mean), ] ) do.call(rbind, best_by_index)[, c("similarity", "num_comp", "localization", "mean", "std_err")] #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   similarity num_comp localization  mean std_err #>   <chr>         <int>        <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl> #> 1 covariance       10          0.5  1.69   0.175 #> 2 euclidean        10          0.5  1.66   0.156

lwplsda_wflow,   resamples = para_folds,   grid = data.frame(localization = 2^seq(-6, 5)),   metrics = metric_set(roc_auc, accuracy) )  show_best(lwplsda_res, metric = "roc_auc", n = 3) #> # A tibble: workflow(     class ~ .,     lwpls(num_comp = 2, localization = 1e6) |> set_mode("classification")   ) |>   last_fit(para_split, metrics = metric_set(roc_auc, accuracy))  rbind(   data.frame(model = "LW-PLS-DA", collect_metrics(lwplsda_final)),   data.frame(model = "Global PLS-DA", collect_metrics(plsda_final)) )[, c("model", ".metric", ".estimate")] #>           model  .metric .estimate #> 1     LW-PLS-DA accuracy 0.9200000 #> 2     LW-PLS-DA  roc_auc 0.9728484 #> 3 Global PLS-DA accuracy 0.6640000 #> 4 Global PLS-DA  roc_auc 0.7612705 para_grid <- expand.grid(   X1 = seq(min(parabolic$X1), max(parabolic$X1), length.out = 100),   X2 = seq(min(parabolic$X2), max(parabolic$X2), length.out = 100) )  region_probs <- function(final, model) {   probs <- predict(extract_workflow(final), para_grid, type = "prob")   data.frame(para_grid, model = model, .pred_Class1 = probs$.pred_Class1) }  regions <- rbind(   region_probs(plsda_final, "Global PLS-DA"),   region_probs(lwplsda_final, "LW-PLS-DA") )  ggplot(regions, aes(X1, X2)) +   geom_raster(aes(fill = .pred_Class1), alpha = 0.8) +   geom_contour(aes(z = .pred_Class1), breaks = 0.5, color = "black") +   geom_point(data = para_test, aes(shape = class), color = "white", size = 2.6) +   geom_point(data = para_test, aes(shape = class, color = class), size = 1.6) +   facet_wrap(~model) +   scale_fill_distiller(palette = title: Robust and sparse LW-PLS
text: LW-PLS already gives tiny weights training samples far query, outliers far away little influence. Outliers among neighbors query different matter: wrong reference value (vertical outlier) unusual spectrum (leverage point) close query enters local model large weight. robust = TRUE, every local model fitted partial robust M-regression (PRM; Serneels et al., 2005). training sample gets weight \[ \omega_i \, w_i^r \, w_i^t, \] product similarity weight \(\omega_i\), weight \(w_i^r\) decreases residual local model, weight \(w_i^t\) decreases distance center local scores. local model refitted new weights stable. weights come Fair function (default) Hampel function (weight_function = "hampel"), gives zero weight outlying samples. medians PRM uses weighted similarity weights, robust model stays local.

code: contaminate <- function(data, fraction, seed = 1) {   set.seed(seed)   bad <- sample(nrow(data), round(fraction * nrow(data)))   shift <- sample(c(-1, 1), length(bad), replace = TRUE) * runif(length(bad), 15, 30)   data$water[bad] <- data$water[bad] + shift   data }  meats_train_20 <- contaminate(meats_train, 0.2) set.seed(2) folds_20 <- vfold_cv(meats_train_20, v = 5) grid <- expand.grid(num_comp = c(4, 6, 8, 10, 12), localization = c(0.5, 1, 2, 4))  tune_lwpls <- function(robust) {   wflow <- workflow(     water ~ .,     lwpls(num_comp = tune(), localization = tune()) |>       set_mode("regression") |>       set_engine("lwpls", robust = robust)   )   res <- tune_grid(wflow, folds_20, grid = grid, metrics = metric_set(trimmed_rmse))   finalize_workflow(wflow, select_best(res, metric = "trimmed_rmse")) }  lwpls_wflow <- tune_lwpls(robust = FALSE) robust_wflow <- tune_lwpls(robust = TRUE) fractions <- c(0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3) test_rmse <- function(wflow, fraction) {   fitted <- fit(wflow, contaminate(meats_train, fraction))   rmse_vec(meats_test$water, predict(fitted, meats_test)$.pred) }  results <- data.frame(   fraction = rep(fractions, 2),   model = rep(c("LW-PLS", "Robust LW-PLS"), each = length(fractions)),   rmse = c(     vapply(fractions, test_rmse, numeric(1), wflow = lwpls_wflow),     vapply(fractions, test_rmse, numeric(1), wflow = robust_wflow)   ) ) results #>   fraction         model     rmse #> 1      0.0        LW-PLS 2.583581 #> 2      0.1        LW-PLS 3.101320 #> 3      0.2        LW-PLS 3.478736 #> 4      0.3        LW-PLS 3.869655 #> 5      0.0 Robust LW-PLS 2.418944 #> 6      0.1 Robust LW-PLS 2.354993 #> 7      0.2 Robust LW-PLS 2.501034 #> 8      0.3 Robust LW-PLS 2.865060 ggplot(results, aes(100 * fraction, rmse, color = model)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +   geom_point(size = 2) +   scale_color_manual(values = c("LW-PLS" = "#969696", "Robust LW-PLS" = "#08519C")) +   labs(     x = "Wrong reference values in the training set (%)",     y = "Test RMSE (water, %)",     color = NULL   ) +   theme_bw()

title: Robust and sparse LW-PLS
text: sparsity \(\eta > 0\), local models fitted sparse NIPALS (SNIPLS; Hoffmann et al., 2015): weight vector component soft-thresholded \(\eta \max_j |w_j|\), predictors small weights dropped. local model selects predictors, wavelengths matter around query. sparsity tuning parameter:  Moderate thresholds keep accuracy dense local models dropping wavelengths small weights ; large thresholds drop much information. Sparse models without robustness give numbers components single fit, tuning num_comp costs nothing extra.

title: Locally-Weighted Partial Least Squares for tidymodels
text: lwpls implements locally-weighted partial least squares (LW-PLS) tidymodels ecosystem. LW-PLS just--time learning method used chemometrics process monitoring (soft sensors). Instead fitting single global model, builds dedicated weighted PLS model around new sample, every training sample weighted similarity sample. linear method can therefore capture nonlinear time-varying relationships.

title: Locally-Weighted Partial Least Squares for tidymodels
text: lwpls(): parsnip model regression (one outcomes) classification (LW-PLS-DA). Two similarity indexes: Euclidean distance original LW-PLS, covariance-based index CbLW-PLS (similarity = "covariance"). Robust local models, partial robust M-regression (set_engine("lwpls", robust = TRUE)), sparse local models select predictors (sparsity), trimmed_rmse() metric tune robust models contaminated data. native implementation, validated Kaneko’s reference implementation, prediction kernel written C++ (RcppArmadillo). Queries processed blocks, work runs BLAS matrix-matrix products. Tuning tune dials: localization() similarity() tuning parameters, values num_comp evaluated single fit (“submodel trick”). lwpls_fit(): standalone hardhat modeling function matrix, data frame, formula recipe interfaces.

code: library(tidymodels) library(lwpls)  data(meats, package = "modeldata") meats <- meats |> select(-fat, -protein)  set.seed(123) meats_split <- initial_split(meats, prop = 0.75) meats_folds <- vfold_cv(training(meats_split), v = 5)  lwpls_wflow <- workflow(   water ~ .,   lwpls(num_comp = tune(), localization = tune()) |> set_mode("regression") )  lwpls_grid <- grid_regular(   num_comp(c(1, 15)),   localization(),   levels = c(num_comp = 15, localization = 8) )  lwpls_res <- tune_grid(lwpls_wflow, meats_folds, grid = lwpls_grid) show_best(lwpls_res, metric = "rmse", n = 3) #> # A tibble: 3 × 8 #>   num_comp localization .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err .config           #>      <int>        <dbl> <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>             #> 1       10          0.5 rmse    standard    1.66     5   0.156 pre0_mod077_post0 #> 2       13          0.5 rmse    standard    1.68     5   0.198 pre0_mod101_post0 #> 3        9          0.5 rmse    standard    1.70     5   0.174 pre0_mod069_post0 lwpls_wflow |>   finalize_workflow(select_best(lwpls_res, metric = "rmse")) |>   last_fit(meats_split) |>   collect_metrics() #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   .metric .estimator .estimate .config         #>   <chr>   <chr>          <dbl> <chr>           #> 1 rmse    standard       1.38  pre0_mod0_post0 #> 2 rsq     standard       0.978 pre0_mod0_post0

title: lwpls: Locally-Weighted Partial Least Squares for 'tidymodels' — lwpls-package
text: Locally-weighted partial least squares (LW-PLS) just--time learning method builds dedicated weighted partial least squares model around every new sample, training samples weighted similarity sample (Kim et al. (2011) doi:10.1016/j.ijpharm.2011.10.007 ). Regression (single multiple outcomes) classification (locally weighted partial least squares-discriminant analysis; Bevilacqua Marini (2014) doi:10.1016/j.aca.2014.05.057 ) supported. local models can robust outliers, partial robust M-regression (Serneels et al. (2005) doi:10.1016/j.chemolab.2005.04.007 ), sparse (Hoffmann et al. (2015) doi:10.1016/j.chemolab.2015.09.019 ). prediction kernel written C++ 'RcppArmadillo', model integrated 'parsnip', 'dials', 'tune' 'yardstick' packages can used within 'tidymodels' framework.

title: Locally-weighted partial least squares — lwpls
text: lwpls() defines locally-weighted partial least squares (LW-PLS) model use parsnip package. LW-PLS just--time (lazy) learner: instead fitting one global model, dedicated weighted PLS model built around every new sample, training sample weighted similarity sample. lets linear method capture nonlinear time-varying relationships, makes popular soft sensors spectroscopic calibration. model can used regression (one numeric outcomes) classification (discriminant analysis class indicators). local models can also sparse, one selects predictors, robust outliers training data. single engine, "lwpls", implemented package (C++ via RcppArmadillo).

code: lwpls(num_comp = 3, localization = 0.5) |>   parsnip::set_mode("regression") |>   parsnip::translate() #> Locally-Weighted PLS Model Specification (regression) #>  #> Main Arguments: #>   num_comp = 3 #>   localization = 0.5 #>  #> Computational engine: lwpls  #>  #> Model fit template: #> lwpls::lwpls_fit(x = missing_arg(), y = missing_arg(), num_comp = 3,  #>     localization = 0.5)  lwpls_mod <-   lwpls(num_comp = 3, localization = 0.5) |>   parsnip::set_mode("regression") |>   parsnip::fit(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars[-(1:5), ])  lwpls_mod #> parsnip model object #>  #> Locally-weighted PLS (regression) #>  #> Training samples: 27  #> Predictors:       10 (standardized)  #> Components:       3  #> Localization:     0.5  #> Similarity:       Euclidean  #> Neighbors:        all (27)  predict(lwpls_mod, new_data = mtcars[1:5, ]) #> # A tibble: 5 × 1 #>   .pred #>   <dbl> #> 1  21.1 #> 2  20.7 #> 3  27.0 #> 4  18.8 #> 5  17.4  # Robust and sparse local models lwpls(num_comp = 3, sparsity = 0.3) |>   parsnip::set_mode("regression") |>   parsnip::set_engine("lwpls", robust = TRUE) |>   parsnip::fit(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars[-(1:5), ]) |>   predict(new_data = mtcars[1:5, ]) #> # A tibble: 5 × 1 #>   .pred #>   <dbl> #> 1  20.3 #> 2  20.7 #> 3  25.2 #> 4  18.6 #> 5  16.0  # Classification lwpls(num_comp = 2) |>   parsnip::set_mode("classification") |>   parsnip::fit(Species ~ ., data = iris) |>   predict(new_data = iris[c(1, 51, 101), ], type = "prob") #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>   .pred_setosa .pred_versicolor .pred_virginica #>          <dbl>            <dbl>           <dbl> #> 1      0.990            0.00970           0     #> 2      0.0269           0.502             0.471 #> 3      0.00553          0.0235            0.971

title: lwpls (development version)
text: Robust LW-PLS: robust = TRUE (engine argument lwpls() argument lwpls_fit()), local model fitted partial robust M-regression (PRM; Serneels et al., 2005), Fair (default) Hampel weight function. medians L1-median PRM uses weighted similarity weights, robust models stay local. Robust models available regression one outcomes classification, standardize data scale distances median MAD. Sparse LW-PLS: new sparsity argument (tunable main argument lwpls(), dials parameter sparsity()) fits local models sparse NIPALS (SNIPLS; Hoffmann et al., 2015), local model selects predictors. Combined robust = TRUE, gives local sparse PRM (SPRM). New yardstick metric trimmed_rmse() tune robust models data outliers. New vignette, vignette("robust-sparse").

title: lwpls 0.2.0

title: lwpls 0.2.0
text: lwpls() now arguments mode, num_comp, localization, neighbors, similarity engine. shapefactor argument replaced localization, parameter similarity function Kim et al. (2011) (lambda Kaneko’s implementation). engine now "lwpls" ("rnirs"). magrittr pipe %>% generics::tidy() longer re-exported. Use native pipe |> (R >= 4.1.0).

title: lwpls 0.2.0
text: Native implementation LW-PLS, validated Kaneko’s reference implementation. prediction kernel written C++ (RcppArmadillo): uses kernel PLS algorithm Dayal & MacGregor (1997) processes queries blocks work runs BLAS matrix-matrix products. Regression one numeric outcomes, classification (LW-PLS-DA) class probability predictions. New lwpls_fit(), hardhat-based fitting function matrix, data frame, formula recipe interfaces. predict() method returns tibbles follow tidymodels conventions can use number components. multi_predict() min_grid() methods: tune evaluates values num_comp single model fit. New dials tuning parameter localization(). Covariance-based LW-PLS (CbLW-PLS, Hazama Kano, 2015): new similarity argument measures similarity samples Euclidean distance ("euclidean", default) along covariance direction training data ("covariance"). can tuned new dials parameter similarity(). optional neighbors argument restricts local model nearest training samples. "lwpls" engine scale argument switch standardization data. Added unit tests (test coverage tracked Codecov) introductory vignette (vignette("lwpls")), including regression classification examples.
